Accessed September 4, 2014. |website = {{URL|https://www.parsippany.net}} |footnotes = }} '''Parsippany–Troy Hills''', commonly known as '''Parsippany''' ({{IPAc-en|p|ɑr|ˈ|s|ɪ|p|ə|n|i}} {{respell|par|SIP|ə|nee}}), is a [[Township (New Jersey)|township]] in [[Morris County, New Jersey|Morris County]], in the [[North Jersey|northern]] portion of the [[U.S. state]] of [[New Jersey]]. As of the [https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/parsippanytroyhillstownshipmorriscountynewjersey/PST045225#PST045225 2025 U.S Census Bureau], the township's population was 56,633. An increase of 2,924 (+5.5%) from the [[2010 United States census|2010 census]] count of 53,238, which in turn had reflected an increase of 2,589 (+5.1%) from the 50,649 counted at the [[2000 United States census|2000 census]].[https://www.nj.gov/labor/labormarketinformation/assets/PDFs/census/2010/2010data/table7cm.xls Table 7. Population for the Counties and Municipalities in New Jersey: 1990, 2000 and 2010], [[New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development]], February 2011. Accessed May 1, 2023. The name ''Parsippany'' comes from the [[Lenape]] [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] sub-tribe, which comes from the word ''parsipanong'', which means "the place where the river winds through the valley."Cheslow, Jerry. [https://www.nytimes.com/1992/02/23/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-of-living-in-parsippany-troy-hills.html "If You're Thinking of Living in: Parsippany–Troy Hills"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', February 23, 1992. Accessed August 7, 2013.Hutchinson, Viola L. [http://mapmaker.rutgers.edu/356/nj_place_names_origin.pdf#page=23 ''The Origin of New Jersey Place Names''], New Jersey Public Library Commission, May 1945. Accessed September 12, 2015. Parsippany–Troy Hills is the most populous municipality in Morris County.[http://www.co.morris.nj.us/history/history.asp The Land Past and Present] ({{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090822123842/http://co.morris.nj.us/history/history.asp |date=August 22, 2009 }}), [[Morris County, New Jersey]]. Accessed August 19, 2007. The name Troy Hills was changed from Troy to avoid confusion of mail being sent erroneously to [[Troy, New York]].Parsippany Historical and Preservation Society. [https://books.google.com/books?id=cSvIfQrfJPEC&pg=PA27 ''Parsippany–Troy Hills''], p. 27. [[Arcadia Publishing]], 1997. {{ISBN|9780738589633}}. Accessed September 12, 2015. Parsippany–Troy Hills was incorporated as a township by an act of the [[New Jersey Legislature]] on March 12, 1928, from portions of [[Hanover Township, New Jersey|Hanover Township]], based on the results of a referendum held on May 9, 1928, that split off both [[East Hanover Township, New Jersey|East Hanover Township]] and Parsippany–Troy Hills from Hanover Township.Snyder, John P. [https://nj.gov/dep/njgs/enviroed/oldpubs/bulletin67.pdf ''The Story of New Jersey's Civil Boundaries: 1606-1968''], Bureau of Geology and Topography; Trenton, New Jersey; 1969. p. 195. Accessed May 30, 2024.Staff. [https://www.nytimes.com/1928/05/10/archives/new-montclair-board-organizes-next-week-cg-phillips-only-candidate.html "New Montclair Board Organizes Next Week – C.G. Phillips Only Candidate to Get First Choice Majority – Three Re-elected at Long Branch"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', May 10, 1928. Accessed October 27, 2018. "The electorate of the present Hanover Township near here turned out in force today and by a vote of 1,938 to 987 registered its approval of the proposal to split the township into three new townships. The present township will be divided into the townships of Parsippany–Troy Hills, East Hanover and Old Township."[http://mclib.info/reference/local-history-genealogy/historical-timeline-of-morris-county-boundaries/ Historical Timeline of Morris County Boundaries] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225144924/http://mclib.info/reference/local-history-genealogy/historical-timeline-of-morris-county-boundaries/ |date=December 25, 2016 }}, Morris County Library. Accessed December 24, 2016. "1928, March 12. Parsippany–Troy Hills Township is established from Hanover Township. From PL 1928, p. 893." Since 2006, Parsippany–Troy Hills appeared eight times on ''[[Money (magazine)|Money]]'' magazine's list of "Best Places to Live in the United States", ranking 17th-best in 2006, 13th-best in 2008, 15th-best in 2012, 17th-best in 2014, fifth-best in 2016, 33rd-best in 2017,{{Cite web |last=Auriemma |first=Adam |date=September 18, 2017 |title=Parsippany-Troy Hills, New Jersey Ranked No.33; Best Places to Live 2017 |url=https://money.com/collection/best-places-to-live-2017/4932831/parsippany-troy-hills-new-jersey-2/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429124931/https://money.com/collection/best-places-to-live-2017/4932831/parsippany-troy-hills-new-jersey-2/ |archive-date=April 29, 2022 |access-date=September 18, 2017 |magazine=Money}}{{Cite web |last=Auriemma |first=Adam |date=September 17, 2018 |title=Parsippany-Troy Hills, New Jersey Ranked No. 26; Best Places to Live 2018 |url=https://money.com/collection/2018-best-places-to-live/5361475/parsippany-troy-hills-new-jersey-3/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220227091012/https://money.com/collection/2018-best-places-to-live/5361475/parsippany-troy-hills-new-jersey-3/ |archive-date=February 27, 2022 |magazine=Money}}{{Cite web |title=Parsippany–Troy Hills |url=https://fortune.com/well/ranking/best-places-families/2022/parsippany-troy-hills/ |access-date=November 27, 2022 |magazine=Fortune |language=en}} 26th-best in 2018, and 15th-best in 2022.[https://web.archive.org/web/20060813114953/http://money.cnn.com/magazines/moneymag/bplive/2006/top100/index.html "Best Places to Live 2006"] (), ''[[Money (magazine)|Money]]'' magazine.
